survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2024 United States note reports descriptive percentages and statistically significant differences/changes based on the TALIS 2024 Database for lower secondary teachers and principals. The excerpt does not specify whether complex survey weights and replicate weights were applied in the production of the published estimates, nor does it name any weight variables. For TALIS analyses, users should apply the official TALIS sampling weights (and replicate weights if variance estimation is required) provided in the TALIS 2024 microdata to account for the multistage sampling design and clustering of teachers within schools. Because this note is a results summary rather than a re-estimation study, the manuscript excerpt does not document any additional preprocessing beyond using the OECD-provided tables for the specified indicators.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This note is a descriptive results brief based on TALIS self-reports (teachers’ and principals’ perceptions and practices) and does not model cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the reported indicators. The excerpt also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure because it relies on OECD-produced tables; therefore, the specific approach to non-response or item non-response is not documented in the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note presents findings based on TALIS 2024 responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals in the United States, and it compares them to an OECD average computed from participating OECD countries and territories with available data. The excerpt does not specify additional analytic restrictions (e.g., grade bands beyond lower secondary, school types, or exclusions for non-response), and it does not report the final analytic sample size.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD note summarizes TALIS 2024 results for the United States, focusing on lower secondary teachers and principals. It reports percentages for teachers’ background (age, gender, non-teaching work experience), teaching for today’s world (adaptation to cultural diversity, collaboration), student diversity and special education needs contexts, social and emotional skills, and technology use (including AI use in the prior 12 months). It also covers teachers’ learning opportunities (initial teacher education quality, induction/mentoring, professional learning impact, needs, and barriers), teacher leadership and autonomy, professional relationships (with teachers, principals, students, and parents/guardians), status of the profession, employment terms, demands/stress sources, appraisal practices, professional outcomes (lesson aims), and well-being/satisfaction/retention intentions. The note explicitly comments only on statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average and does not provide model-based ML performance metrics or causal estimates.

The appropriate extraction is to document the assessment scope (TALIS 2024, lower secondary teachers/principals, United States) and the descriptive indicator set reported in the OECD tables.
